title: [Viewpoint] The clinician–artificial intelligence scientist: a proposed career pathway in medicine
desc: Traditionally, the clinician–scientist has played a key role in translating fundamental discoveries into clinical practice across multiple medical disciplines. As medicine enters the era of artificial intelligence (AI), a similar role is needed to bridge the gap between technological development and meaningful clinical implementation—a role we term the clinician–AI scientist. In this Viewpoint, we examine the distinctive role, challenges, and development strategies of this potentially new career pathway for clinicians.

title: Gut and urogenital microbiomes influence menopausal hormone therapy outcomes
desc: A 6-month study shows that menopausal hormone therapy induces multi-site microbiome remodeling, including rejuvenation of the vaginal microbial community toward a reproductive-age-like state. In turn, baseline gut and vaginal community types affect the clinical response to therapy. Integrating clinical and gut microbiome features predicts rapid symptom remission, providing a blueprint for precision menopausal care.

title: Speak before the reveal: a practical method to protect clinical reasoning from artificial intelligence scribe deskilling, never-skilling, and mis-skilling.
source: PubMed · Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
desc: [Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA] Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes are rapidly becoming normalized in clinical practice, yet governance frameworks focus on accuracy, privacy, consent, and medicolegal status. Risks to clinician capabilities have received less attention. Speak before the reveal is a proposed method in which clinicians verbalize critical cognitive steps, such as synthesis and plan, before note generation. Recent work distinguishes deskilling in senior clinicians, never-skilling from premature offload in trainees and mis-skilling, the internalization of AI errors and inappropriate use as sound practice. This Perspective builds on emerging evidence that reasoning before seeing AI output may protect unaided reasoning. Training implementation, evaluation, adherence challenges, validation methodology, and governance strategies for training bodies, health services, and scribe vendors are discussed. Speak before the reveal is a low-cost, testable approach to maintaining clinical reasoning for individuals or organizations. Successful AI scribe adoption requires preserving clinicians' ability to work without AI support.

title: DeepTNR: predicting tumor drug sensitivity from spatial transcriptomics with deep graph contrastive and transfer learning
desc: Heterogeneity within the tumor microenvironment remains a major obstacle to precision oncology. Although existing drug-sensitivity models can capture transcriptional heterogeneity, they generally do not account for the spatial organization of predicted drug responses. Here, we developed DeepTNR, a spatially resolved framework that integrates tumor-stroma interface features, spatial autocorrelation, and distance-dependent associations between local cellular composition and predicted drug sensitivity. Across nine tumor types, with colorectal cancer (CRC) as a representative example, DeepTNR identified irinotecan as the most sensitive drug and revealed significant spatial autocorrelation in its predicted response patterns. Spatial proximity effect analysis further showed that local enrichment of immune and proliferative programs positively was associated with increased irinotecan sensitivity. Together, these findings demonstrate the potential of DeepTNR to resolve intratumoral therapeutic heterogeneity and identify niche-specific vulnerabilities.

title: [Articles] Detecting low left ventricular ejection fraction from ECG using an interpretable and scalable predictor-driven framework: a model development and validation study
desc: Diagnostic scores of conventional ECG findings from ECG foundation models contain information relevant to the detection of ventricular dysfunction. These representations can be directly reused for low LVEF detection and further integrated into interpretable predictive models, providing a scalable and extensible computational framework for existing AI-ECG systems. Future research should validate the framework in population-based screening settings and larger international cohorts.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Nursing Care Decision-Making: A Randomized Controlled Trial
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Chimei Medical Center; conditions: Nursing Care Planning; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 120; status: COMPLETED] This study evaluates whether assistance from a large language model (LLM), a type of artificial intelligence that generates text, improves the quality of nursing care plans and reduces the time needed to complete them. The study included 120 registered nurses working in internal medicine wards, surgical wards, and intensive care units at a medical center in southern Taiwan. Nurses were randomly assigned to one of two groups: * Independent planning: Nurses prepared, reviewed, and submitted a care plan without LLM assistance. * LLM-assisted planning: Nurses entered prompts to obtain an LLM-generated draft, then reviewed and revised the draft before submitting their final care plan. Each nurse completed only the assigned workflow during a single study session. Participants completed a brief baseline questionnaire and prepared nursing problems, goals, and interventions for a standardized simulated clinical case. Tasks were performed in a secure hospital test environment without real patient data. Expert nurse raters who were not informed of group assignments independently evaluated the final care plans. The nursing care decision quality assessment has a maximum total score of 30 points, comprising decision-content quality (25 points) and decision-language quality (5 points). The system recorded task completion time. Researchers compare the two groups' final care-plan quality scores and task completion times.

title: Artificial intelligence in dermatophytosis: Toward better clinical diagnosis and management.
desc: [Journal de mycologie medicale] Dermatophytosis is one of the most common superficial fungal infections worldwide. However, its diagnosis and management remain challenging because its clinical manifestations often overlap with those of other dermatoses, conventional mycological tests have inherent limitations, the disease is prone to recurrence, and antifungal resistance has received increasing attention. This review summarizes current applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in dermatophytosis, with a focus on the use of machine learning and deep learning in clinical photographs, non-invasive skin imaging, and laboratory diagnostics, while also discussing their roles in treatment support, follow-up assessment, patient education, and adherence management. In addition, with the accumulation of molecular diagnostic, mass spectrometric, and epidemiological data, AI may also provide auxiliary support for extended applications such as resistance risk recognition. Current evidence suggests that AI can improve the efficiency, consistency, and objectivity of dermatophytosis diagnosis and provide quantitative support for treatment response assessment and long-term follow-up. With further improvement in research quality and the accumulation of clinical application experience, AI is expected to become increasingly integrated into dermatophytosis management workflows.

title: Mixed Signals: Weight-Space Programming for EEG and ECG
desc: Weight-space programming allows language models to read a trained neural network's weights and edit them. This opens the door to ``training'' by reasoning rather than through gradient descent. Prior work has demonstrated its functionality and promise for game-playing networks and fixing specific failures in language models, even extending to diffusion models. In this work, we present its applicability to models trained on biosignal data, specifically EEG and ECG data. We show that frontier models are not only able to debug specific faults planted in biosignal-based models without being told what these faults are, but are even capable of writing all the weights of a network from scratch, given only the architecture, the task, and a minimal set of training subjects. In particular, in one set of experiments, a language model was able to match standard gradient-descent training using 6times fewer training subjects, through reasoning alone and without any gradient descent step. Networks written by Claude Opus 5.5 also scored higher than classic hand-crafted EEG pipelines (alpha band power, and common spatial patterns with linear discriminant analysis) when built from the same 5 subjects. We also highlight some of the limitations, which include the inability of language models to improve already well-trained classification models, and their incapacity to reliably recognize, from the weights alone, the task a network was trained on. Overall, our results indicate that weight-space programming can be useful for small networks, such as those deployed on edge devices and wearables, but the concept still requires further investigation before it can be used in practice.

title: A frontier machine intelligence for human neuroimaging
desc: Medical imaging is essential for diagnosing disease, guiding treatment and monitoring patients over time. Although artificial intelligence has advanced image interpretation, existing medical models often address restricted tasks, while general-purpose proprietary models lack access to private clinical imaging required to achieve medical expertise. Developing models that can interpret complex examinations and communicate their findings in the context of clinical decisions remains a major challenge. Here, we show that Neuro-VL, a vision-language model trained on nearly one million neuroimaging studies from routine clinical care, can interpret complete imaging examinations and engage in natural language conversations about their findings. Across internal and international datasets, Neuro-VL outperformed frontier general-purpose and specialized medical models in diagnosing, localizing, and describing abnormalities, as well as generating comprehensive radiology reports. The model also compared serial examinations to assess disease progression and more reliably resisted misleading clinical assumptions than leading frontier models from OpenAI and Google. These results extend health system learning beyond individual predictions to interactive image interpretation and longitudinal disease monitoring. They demonstrate how the collective clinical experience of health systems can be used to develop medical AI with specialized expertise and broad clinical capabilities.

title: MENTOR: An Evidence-Informed Large Language Model-Based Multi-Agent System for Efficient Selection of Institution-Specific Negative Control Outcomes
desc: Objective Negative control outcomes (NCOs) help detect and correct systematic error in observational studies, yet their selection remains largely manual. The Common Evidence Model (CEM) can generate candidate lists, but researchers must still screen them for plausibility as true nulls and for sufficient observation in each institution's data. We developed and evaluated MENTOR (Multi-agent Evidence-informed Negative conTrol Outcome selection with Reasoning), a multi-agent system of large language models (LLMs) that combines CEM evidence with LLM reasoning to select institution-specific NCOs. Methods Four LLM agents operate on an institution's Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership common data model. A Curator summarizes drug labels, a Suggester assesses locally frequent candidates with CEM evidence and a first-pass LLM judgment, an Adjudicator resolves their disagreements, and a Diagnostician relaxes the patient-count threshold until a target number of NCOs is met. Using Qwen3.6-27B, we evaluated 349 candidates for three drug pairs in a Korean tertiary hospital's electronic health records (2.9 million patients) against a blinded LLM judge from a different model family, validated by three experts on 90 candidates. We compared accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), and sensitivity with CEM-only and first-pass-LLM-only selection. Results MENTOR proposed 243 NCOs versus 121 by CEM-only, with higher accuracy (0.83 [0.79-0.87] vs. 0.53 [0.48-0.58]), sensitivity (0.89 vs. 0.41), and PPV (0.86 vs. 0.79). Judge-expert agreement was {kappa}=0.63. Adjudication, needed for 44.1% of candidates, added little accuracy, and only with reasoning mode. Concordant acceptances, which bypass it, contained about half of the false positives. Only 7%-9% of CEM-proposed outcomes had at least 10,000 patients at the institution. Conclusion Combining LLM judgments with CEM evidence and local data yielded more NCOs, with higher PPV, than CEM alone. Restricting reasoning to discordant candidates kept computation time below 40% of that with reasoning in all agents. Every decision comes with its evidence and rationale for investigators' final review.

title: Multimodal protein representations across human brain cell types
desc: The central nervous system (CNS) comprises diverse cell types whose molecular context shapes the roles of the proteins they express. Computational models offer a scalable way to study the roles of proteins across human brain cell types, with protein language models and interactome- or single-cell-based models capturing complementary information encoded in protein sequences and cellular network contexts. Human brain tissue is hard to access, so brain cell types make up a small fraction of the atlases single-cell models train on and of the benchmarks used for their evaluation. To capture these complementary sources of information in the CNS, we introduce SEMPER, a multimodal representation learning model that aligns protein language model representations with protein-protein interaction networks from 442 cell types of the adult human brain, giving each protein a sequence-informed representation in every cell type in which its gene is expressed. We show that SEMPER representations predict cell type-specific protein complexes and predict genes essential to the survival of dopaminergic neurons, measured in a genome-wide CRISPR screen. In zero-shot retrieval, SEMPER recovers clinically pursued drug targets for Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis, Huntington's disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis at higher rates than cell type-specific models. To further improve target recovery, we combine SEMPER with a large language model that reasons over protein functional annotations. The combination recovers more targets, with SEMPER providing experimentally derived cellular context that complements literature-based reasoning of the large language model.

title: Effect of two common GVHD prophylaxis regimens on the gut microbiome in a randomized phase 3 trial
desc: In a prespecified companion study (BMT CTN 1801) of the randomized phase 3 BMT CTN 1703 trial comparing two common GVHD prophylaxis regimens, microbiome diversity at engraftment did not associate with non-relapse mortality, but secondary analyses found baseline microbiome diversity was associated with clinical outcomes. Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation can cure certain hematological disorders but has many complications. In retrospective studies, low gut microbiome diversity is associated with adverse clinical outcomes. In 2023, the Blood and Marrow Transplant Clinical Trials Network 1703 randomized phase 3 trial demonstrated the superiority of post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy) and mycophenolate mofetil to tacrolimus and methotrexate (Tac/MTX) for graft-versus-host disease prophylaxis in participants with hematological malignancies undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation. Here we report on the microbiome-focused companion study to 1703, Blood and Marrow Transplant Clinical Trials Network 1801, which coenrolled participants and shared trial registration. The primary endpoint was association between microbiome diversity at neutrophil engraftment and non-relapse mortality after 1 year; secondary endpoints included associations with other clinical outcomes and with baseline microbiome diversity. Based on 2575 longitudinally collected stool samples from 304 participants (Tac/MTX n = 147, PTCy n = 157), no association between engraftment microbiome diversity and non-relapse mortality was observed ( P = 0.314), not meeting the primary endpoint. Lower baseline microbiome diversity was associated with shorter overall survival ( P = 0.007). Safety data were reported in the original 1703 publication. In exploratory analyses, microbiome diversity and absolute microbial load were lower in PTCy compared to Tac/MTX on days 14–28 following HCT, independent of non-prophylaxis antibiotics exposure. Microbial domination events, when a single species exceeds 30% relative abundance, did not differ significantly between study arms and reflected both pathogen blooms and less severe disruptions of the microbial community. Clostridium scindens and secondary bile-acid metabolism pathways were less prevalent in PTCy than in Tac/MTX following HCT. In summary, we find prophylaxis regimens likely exert independent effects on both the microbiome and immune compartments and can also impact their interaction. title: Artificial intelligence methods for HER2 status assessment: a systematic review and diagnostic meta-analysis.
desc: [Abdominal radiology (New York)] Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is an important predictive and prognostic biomarker that guides targeted therapy, particularly in breast and gastric cancers. Conventional HER2 assessment using immunohistochemistry (IHC) and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) is limited by inter-observer variability, heterogeneous expression, and diagnostic complexity. This systematic review and diagnostic meta-analysis followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines to evaluate Artificial Intelligence-based HER2 assessment. Fifty-one studies were included in the qualitative synthesis and 14 in the diagnostic meta-analysis. Bibliometric analysis, methodological taxonomy, comparative evaluation, and pooled diagnostic performance were assessed, with study quality evaluated using QUADAS-2. AI methodologies have rapidly evolved from conventional machine learning and radiomics to deep learning, Vision Transformers, explainable AI, and multimodal frameworks, with histopathology and Magnetic Resonance Imaging. being the most frequently used modalities. Research activity increased markedly between 2023 and 2025. Pooled sensitivity was 87.8%, specificity was 83.5%, and Summary Receiver Operating Characteristic Area Under the Curve (SROC AUC) was 0.852 (95% CI: 0.801-0.881), indicating promising overall diagnostic performance. Deeks' funnel plot asymmetry test showed no significant evidence of publication bias (p = 0.14). However, heterogeneity warrants cautious interpretation of the pooled estimates. Heterogeneous datasets, limited external validation, and inconsistent evaluation methods remain important barriers to clinical implementation. Future research should emphasize multicenter prospective validation, explainable and multimodal AI, foundation models, federated learning, and evaluation in underexplored malignancies, including gallbladder cancer.

title: KQML-Liver: Interpretable Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Liver Disease Classification
desc: Liver disease remains a major global health concern, highlighting the need for reliable and accessible early detection methods. Although recent advances in machine learning, deep learning and quantum machine learning (QML) have introduced promising diagnostic tools, many approaches suffer from limited interpretability and inflated performance caused by data leakage or overly simplistic evaluation protocols. These constraints reduce their reliability in real-world clinical practice. This paper proposes KQML-Liver, a hybrid framework that integrates QML with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) to enhance predictive performance and interpretability. The architecture combines parameterized quantum circuits for expressive feature representation with KAN-based functional mappings that capture nonlinear relationships in an interpretable manner. Evaluated on the Indian Liver Patient Dataset (ILPD) under a rigorous preprocessing protocol preventing data leakage, the proposed model achieves 82% classification accuracy and 100% recall, detecting all positive cases, outperforming existing baselines while providing improved transparency in clinical predictions. These results suggest that hybrid KAN-quantum architectures offer a promising direction for interpretable AI-assisted medical diagnosis.

title: Automating postmarketing pharmacovigilance with large language model agents
desc: Postmarketing pharmacovigilance relies on spontaneous adverse event reporting and labor-intensive observational studies, which suffer from underreporting and delayed risk detection. Large language model (LLM) agents could automate real-world evidence generation, but generalist agents make ad hoc analytical decisions that compromise epidemiological validity and reproducibility. Here we present MedCheckpoint, a multi-agent LLM system for automated postmarketing pharmacovigilance. MedCheckpoint grounds each analytical stage in a curated, source-traceable medical knowledge base, locks core study-design parameters before execution, performs patient-level analyses with human-written deterministic statistical tools, and enforces checkpoint rules that abort infeasible analyses, with optional human-in-the-loop review. We evaluated MedCheckpoint using a 54-question benchmark on a dual-purpose simulated electronic health record (EHR) testbed of 2.7 million individuals, designed with reliable clinical signals to evaluate routine analytical accuracy alongside spurious signals to stress-test system rigor. Across the benchmark, MedCheckpoint outperformed two coding-agent baselines in report quality across five dimensions rated by three independent LLM judges (overall means 4.81-4.88 versus 4.25-4.55 and 4.02-4.29) and yielded higher run-to-run consistency (mean within-question standard deviation 0.116-0.186 versus up to 0.440). Crucially, while baselines failed on up to 2 of 21 runs when handling infeasible comparisons or unmeasurable outcomes, MedCheckpoint produced no misleading failures across all seven stress-test trap questions with known data limitations. MedCheckpoint enables reliable, auditable, and scalable pharmacovigilance analysis.

title: Towards end-to-end LLM-based censoring-aware survival analysis.
desc: [Journal of biomedical informatics] Survival analysis is central to medical prediction, yet large language models (LLMs) are rarely used as end-to-end survival models because censoring prevents straightforward supervised fine-tuning. Here we present LLMSurvival, a framework that enables censoring-aware survival analysis with unmodified LLMs operating directly on tabular clinical data. LLMSurvival reformulates time-to-event prediction as pairwise ranking among comparable subjects, and derives test-time risk by aggregating comparisons against anchor individuals from the training cohort. Across two clinical tasks (ICU mortality prediction in MIMIC-IV and fragility fracture prediction in a NewYork-Presbyterian/Weill Cornell Medicine cohort), LLMSurvival improves overall concordance over Cox proportional hazards modeling by 3.1% for ICU mortality and 0.5% for fracture risk, and by 2.1% on average for ICU mortality and 2.8% for fracture risk over three established deep learning survival models. The results show that survival modeling with censoring can be made compatible with LLM fine-tuning through comparison-based reformulation. The framework demonstrates high portability and superior performance over expert-curated scores like SAPS-II and FRAX scores across diverse clinical contexts. Furthermore, the framework supports local deployment, as compact, publicly available base models provide sufficient performance. The LLMSurvival framework serves as a proof of concept for an integrated, censoring-conscious approach to survival analysis via LLMs.

title: Do Large Language Models Show Racial and Sex Bias in Pain Management? A Counterfactual Audit of GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, DeepSeek and Qwen
desc: Racial and ethnic minority patients receive less pain treatment than non-Hispanic White patients, and large language models (LLMs) used as medical AI could reproduce that bias. Prior audits tested a few proprietary models, stated race explicitly and rarely measured the models' own response instability. In exploratory, non-preregistered analyses, Study 1 had four open-weight LLMs assess six acute-pain vignettes in every combination of four races and two sexes, with identity stated or cued only by a name (two names per group), comparing each identity with a White male reference on the same case and sampling seed. In Study 2, 24 configurations of 17 models, including OpenAI's GPT-4.1 mini and gpt-oss, Anthropic's Claude Haiku 4.5, Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash, Meta's Llama, DeepSeek and Qwen, with reasoning on and off and at two precisions, answered the same vignettes and the 50 clinician-written Q-Pain cases. In this single-prompt, JSON-constrained task, no difference survived correction in Study 1, none of 1,386 comparisons survived the false discovery rate in Study 2, and every pain-severity difference was equivalent to zero within one point on a 0-10 scale (within a quarter point for 237 of 238 Q-Pain comparisons). Opioid decisions were bounded less precisely (Study 1 could not exclude differences of about 20 percentage points), so they show no detected difference, not proof of none. The few differences surviving correction within a model favoured Black patients. Models differed far more from one another and across their own settings than between patients (the reference patient received the high opioid dose in 6% to 93% of responses), although serving software, provider and prompt format also differed. Fairness audits of clinical AI should use several names per group, pair comparisons on the seed, report the noise floor and test each deployed configuration.

title: Detecting Contradictory Evidence on Drug-Disease Associations at Scale
desc: Contradictory claims about drug efficacy across randomized controlled trials (RCTs) complicate evidence-based medicine, yet existing automated methods classify isolated sentence pairs and do not explain why studies disagree. We present DrugCon, a large language model (LLM)-based framework that extracts study conclusions from RCT abstracts, links these claims when they concern the same drug-disease association, detects contradictions with counterfactual reasoning, and explains them using a taxonomy of ten study-level factors such as population, dosage, and outcome measures. Applying DrugCon to 224,756 RCT abstracts, we built DrugCon-Bench, an exhaustively annotated benchmark of 542 contradictory claim pairs from 819 abstracts. Most contradictions involve more than one study-level factor (75.5%). The most common are differences in outcome measures (64.0%), populations (51.3%), and dosage or exposure duration (35.6%). DrugCon achieves an F1 score of 0.744 for contradiction detection, outperforming rule-based, supervised, and natural language inference baselines, and an F1 of 0.482 for identifying explanatory study factors. DrugCon enables scalable and explainable analysis of contradictory clinical evidence.

desc: Colluding on unsanctioned message boards and infiltrating a technology platform. Hacking the statistics portal of a health care scheme. title: Prompt design in large language model health coaching chatbots: A scoping review.
desc: [PLOS digital health] Artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are being explored to deliver health coaching across multiple contexts. However, the quality and safety of chatbot-generated advice is influenced by how prompts are constructed, and prompt design remains inconsistently described in the literature. This scoping review examined how prompt design has been applied and evaluated in AI health coaching chatbots and summarized the study designs, prompt strategies, and outcomes reported across studies. We conducted a scoping review following PRISMA-ScR guidance and searched PubMed, Embase/Ovid MEDLINE ALL, PsycINFO, IEEE Xplore, and Scopus for peer-reviewed studies published up to October 2025. Eligible studies examined prompt design in large language model-based health coaching chatbots. Data were extracted using a standardized form and synthesized narratively. Twelve studies were included, spanning mental health, medication use, physical activity, and nutrition contexts. Study designs were primarily simulation-based, with few involving real users. Prompt strategies were grouped into structural modifications, prompting techniques, and role-based approaches. Structural modifications, such as increasing specificity and adding constraints, were most common and were reported to improve response quality and clarity. Prompting techniques were reported to improve task performance but sometimes reduced focus or consistency. Role-based prompting influenced tone, specificity, and guideline alignment. Outcomes focused mainly on response quality, with fewer studies assessing safety or user experience and only one evaluating clinical outcomes. Prompt design is a key, modifiable determinant of chatbot performance. However, current evidence is limited by heterogeneous study designs and minimal real-world evaluation. Greater focus on prompt design is needed to improve the quality and safety of AI-delivered health coaching and its real-world impact on health outcomes.

title: Supervision-Aware Evaluation of MedGemma for Reference-Assisted Radiotherapy Contour Ranking
desc: Radiotherapy contour ranking can support quality assurance, but vision-language model (VLM) gains may reflect supervision, score construction, available inputs, or representation access. We evaluated frozen MedGemma 1.5 in a single-institution study, a 12-patient held-out HaN-Seg test, five-fold cross-fitting on 30 non-test HaN-Seg patients, and transfer without refitting to 120 SegRap2023 patients. On held-out HaN-Seg, a supervised readout of the final prompt state exceeded a supervised readout of the model's yes/no output probabilities by +0.3047 pooled average precision (AP; 95% patient-bootstrap interval [+0.2822, +0.3269]); the advantage persisted against a parameter-count-matched nonlinear control. A readout of projected visual tokens exceeded the final-state readout in cross-fitting and transfer (+0.0706 AP averaged equally across patients on SegRap; 95% interval [+0.0607, +0.0804]), while a structured panel-feature readout remained competitive with visual tokens. The anatomy-conditioned readout did not demonstrate an advantage over the native-feature comparator. These results motivate visual-token and structured-feature controls in medical-imaging VLM evaluations; outcomes were computational or synthetic, not clinical acceptability.

title: AToP: An Explainability Framework for Transformer-Based EHR Predictions Using Attribution-Guided Temporal Pattern Mining
desc: Objective: To develop and evaluate AToP (Attribution to Temporal Patterns), a post-hoc explainability framework that converts per-token Integrated Gradients (IG) from a Transformer into structured temporal pattern narratives. Materials and Methods: AToP was applied to a single-stream Transformer trained on MIMIC-IV v3.1 (218,196 patients; 12.6% unplanned 30-day readmission). It mines frequent episodes from salient-token subsequences in the training cohort, aggregates attribution among patients whose records contain each token or pattern, and collapses near-duplicates by patient overlap. Validation used masking, reversed-order analysis, token-level faithfulness tests, and KernelSHAP comparison. Results: The Transformer achieved AUROC 0.77 and PR-AUC 0.34. Population-weighted attribution emphasized high-prevalence codes with small per-patient impact. Carrier-conditional attribution, the mean among patients with the token, surfaced rare high-attribution psychiatric markers including psychosis, self-harm overdose, suicidal ideation (SI), and severe major depressive disorder (MDD). Pattern-level attribution identified within-visit co-occurrences and cross-visit trajectories not captured by token rankings. Risk-increasing patterns included psychiatric sequences ({MDD, SI} [->] SI) and oncologic progressions (cancer anemia [->] ascites). Obstetric and chest pain evaluation patterns were associated with lower predicted readmission. Discussion: The framework provides two complementary views of model predictions: carrier-conditional aggregation highlights rare, highly attributed clinical features, while temporal pattern analysis identifies within-visit combinations and cross-visit trajectories missed by token-level rankings. Masking and visit-order reversal provided evidence of correspondence with model behavior, but pattern attributions do not represent unique effects or establish clinical validity. Conclusion: AToP turns a Transformer's attributions into visit-anchored temporal pattern narratives, showing which events, in which order, contribute to its readmission predictions.

title: Prior-informed machine learning for clinically interpretable medical diagnosis.
source: PubMed · Frontiers in bioengineering and biotechnology
desc: [Frontiers in bioengineering and biotechnology] Traditional machine learning (ML) in medical diagnostics often suffers from limited clinical interpretability and poor generalization, owing to its black-box, data-driven nature. Here, we present Prior-Informed Machine Learning (PIML), a framework that integrates clinically grounded generative reasoning with data-driven, ML-enabled discriminative modeling through Bayesian inference to provide clinically interpretable, patient-specific diagnostic outcomes. By embedding the optimization of sensitivity and specificity in data-driven diagnosis-requirements for subsequent Bayesian inference-directly into the ML model development process, PIML enables a synergistic integration of machine learning and clinical expertise that cannot be achieved through either data-driven or clinically grounded approaches alone. PIML was validated across three clinical domains-cervical neoplasia detection, high-risk oral lesion detection, and preterm birth detection-where Bayesian inference was systematically employed to integrate electrical impedance spectroscopy (EIS)-based machine learning with domain-specific clinical expertise, thereby enabling more comprehensive and enhanced diagnostic decision-making. Our results demonstrate that PIML generally improves diagnostic performance compared with standard ML approaches and provides competitive or superior performance relative to knowledge-based and feature-level prior integration strategies. This work presents an innovative, systematic framework with strong potential for widespread adoption in addressing medical diagnostic challenges across heterogeneous clinical environments.

title: Breath-Dx: A Time Series Classification Benchmark for Disease Screening with eNose
desc: Electronic nose (eNose) technology offers a portable, non-invasive route for disease screening via exhaled breath analysis. However, progress in the field is hindered by the lack of systematic benchmarks that compare machine learning methods under realistic conditions, particularly sensor drift, a known but rarely quantified failure mode. Most existing studies rely on small, private datasets with inconsistent protocols, rendering results non-comparable and slowing progress. We introduce Breath-Dx, the first comprehensive benchmark of time series classification methods for breath-based disease screening. Our work leverages the Scent of Health (S-OH) dataset, the largest public clinical eNose collection to date, comprising 1,234 patients across nine diagnostic groups, each providing a 17-channel multivariate time series with explicit temporal train/test splits that account for sensor drift. We systematically evaluate 10 methods spanning four families: feature-based tabular learners, convolution-based models, graph-based, and time series architectures. All methods degrade significantly under temporal validation (0.05-0.12 AUC drop compared to random cross-validation), confirming that drift embeds a strong temporal signal. Under this realistic evaluation, the best methods achieve ROC AUC of 0.74-0.76 for some lung conditions, though others remain near chance. Recurrent architectures show the most consistent performance across diseases, while specialized time series methods achieve the highest peak results. Demographic confounders matter: breath signals provide independent diagnostic value for some conditions but add little beyond age for others. We release the S-OH dataset, all temporal splits, evaluation protocols, and code to enable reproducible research and accelerate progress in clinical breathomics.

title: Assessment of Undergraduate Psychological Wellbeing Using Explainable Machine Learning: A Study from Sri Lanka
desc: Academic, psychosocial, financial, environmental, and interpersonal factors are widely recognized as important contributors to the overall wellbeing of students. This study aimed to identify factors associated with the psychological wellbeing of university undergraduates and compare the performance of machine learning models for binary and multiclass classification of wellbeing status using self-reported survey data from undergraduates at the University of Peradeniya, Sri Lanka. The findings may facilitate the early identification of students with lower wellbeing and inform targeted interventions to foster a healthier and more supportive academic environment. Cross-sectional questionnaire data from 2,913 undergraduates were analyzed to classify psychological wellbeing using overall happiness scores. Scores were grouped into binary (1-5 and 6-9) and multiclass (1-4, 5-6, and 7-9) categories. Data preprocessing included missing value imputation, one-hot encoding, and feature scaling where appropriate. Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), XGBoost (XGB), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) models were trained using repeated stratified 10-fold cross-validation and evaluated using macro F1-score, ROC-AUC, and classification reports. SHAP analysis was employed to interpret feature contributions and enhance model interpretability. XGB achieved the highest macro-F1 score (70.5%) for binary classification, with a test accuracy of 72.5%. The model correctly classified 63.6% and 80% of participants in the lower and higher psychological wellbeing groups, respectively. For multiclass classification, RF achieved the highest macro-F1 score (54.6%), with a test accuracy of 56.5%. The model correctly classified 48%, 57%, and 60% of participants in the lower, intermediate, and higher psychological wellbeing groups, respectively. SHAP analysis identified academic coping, health and wellbeing, financial circumstances, and interpersonal relationships as key predictors of psychological wellbeing across both models. These findings demonstrate the potential of machine learning to classify psychological wellbeing groups using self-reported data, supporting early identification of students at risk of poor wellbeing and informing targeted university-level mental health interventions.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Precision Phytomedicine: A Critical Review and the Patient-Product-Mechanism-Response (PPMR) Framework.
desc: [Phytotherapy research : PTR] Plant-derived preparations remain widely used, yet their clinical application is constrained by multicomponent composition, batch-to-batch chemical variability, and complex pharmacokinetics, poorly characterized interactions, and marked interindividual variability in response. Artificial intelligence (AI) and computational pharmacology offer analytical tools suited to the high-dimensional data generated by phytomedicine, but enthusiasm has outpaced the supporting evidence. This critical narrative review evaluates AI applications across the phytomedicine pipeline, grading them by the strength and directness of evidence from computational prediction through in vitro, animal, observational, and randomized clinical studies. We organize the field around a Patient-Product-Mechanism-Response (PPMR) framework, arguing that meaningful personalization requires joint characterization of both the patient and the chemically variable botanical product. Current applications are most mature for botanical authentication, spectral annotation, quality assurance, and mechanism-informed hypothesis generation, whereas validated tools for patient stratification, individualized product and dose selection, and improved clinical outcomes remain limited. Rather than claiming efficacy gains, we present AI as a means to advance standardized, mechanism-informed, and testable phytomedicine, contingent on higher-quality data, prospective external validation, and regulatory alignment. The central finding is that none of the studies examined demonstrated a complete AI-guided personalized-phytomedicine pathway from joint patient-and-product characterization through a prospectively validated individualized response; precision phytomedicine should therefore be described as an emerging and hypothesis-generating research programme rather than an established clinical capability.

title: CaseScope: A Multi-Field Benchmark for Case-Level Pathology Diagnosis with Multimodal LLMs
desc: Pathologists rarely diagnose from a single image: they scan a section at low power for architecture, zoom into selected fields for cytology, and integrate the evidence across views and scales. Pathology benchmarks for multimodal large language models (MLLMs), however, mostly ask about one image or require whole-slide pipelines, and the few that show several fields draw nested regions from cancer slides of one public cohort. We introduce CaseScope, a benchmark of diagnosis from several curated fields of one lesion: CaseScope-Teaching, 436 cases from a residency-training image library, reconstructed, de-identified, harmonised against a WHO-based ontology and re-examined by a pathologist wherever an automated pre-review raised a doubt, and CaseScope-Atlas, 800 cases from 88 published atlases (387 of them figure series of one disease), labelled from the captions by two LLMs that must agree. They cover 843 entities across 18 organ systems and pose 4,679 items in six tasks, from open-ended and ten-way diagnosis with ontology-guided hard negatives under circular evaluation to the verification and location of morphological findings. Across twenty-eight open and four proprietary MLLMs, diagnoses are unstable -- the best open and proprietary models are correct under all ten option rotations on 17.9% and 61.7% of the teaching cases -- and wrong answers favour the classic look-alike; open models make little use of the additional fields on teaching cases, where the one-line specimen site matters more, although on atlas cases with three or more fields the fields count about as much as the site; and most open models verify findings barely above chance (median 62.0% vs. 50%, best 81.5%), gaining a median +3.4 points from images; proprietary models reach 83.2-93.2%. Rankings broadly replicate between the sources. The evaluation code is available at https://github.com/Wenchuan-Zhang/CaseScope.

title: Network scaling in swarm learning across real hospitals of different sizes: a KPI-driven analysis on the eICU Collaborative Research Database
desc: Background. Distributed learning lets hospitals train prediction models jointly without exchanging patient records, but how the benefits of a swarm network change as it grows, and which hospitals gain most, have so far been studied with artificial partitions of single-center databases. We examined network scaling on real hospitals that differ in size, volume and sepsis prevalence. Methods. We applied the seven-KPI swarm-learning evaluation framework (Swarm Gain, Local Gain, Relative Local Gain, Model Stability Index, Jain's index, Data Utility Index and label entropy) to progressive network scaling on the eICU Collaborative Research Database. From 25 hospitals (71,887 ICU stays; sepsis prevalence 16.6%), six hospitals stratified by bed size (two small, two medium, two large; 14,776 stays) formed networks of two, four and six hospitals in all six category-joining orders; four further hospitals served as substitutes in robustness checks. Swarm learning was simulated with the client-controlled workflow of NVIDIA FLARE (federated averaging, 30 rounds, five random seeds). The task was whole-stay sepsis classification from discretized vital-sign, laboratory and medication features with a 1,313-parameter feedforward network, with AUROC as the metric. Results. Network AUROC increased with every addition in every ordering, from 0.734 (small-first), 0.755 (medium-first) and 0.781 (large-first) at two hospitals to 0.804 (SD 0.002) at six. Swarm Gain exceeded 1 at all nine unique transitions (mean 1.042 for two-to-four and 1.020 for four-to-six hospitals). Every hospital had Local Gain below 1; relative improvement over local training ranged from 4.1% for the strongest hospital (local AUROC 0.773) to 29.5% for the weakest (0.621), averaging 25.5% for small and 5.9% for large hospitals. Adding large hospitals gave existing members the largest gain (mean Relative Local Gain +6.2%); adding small hospitals never reduced it. Seed-to-seed variability fell from a coefficient of variation of 2.2% at two hospitals to 0.2% at six. Feature distributions were near-identical across hospitals (Data Utility Index 0.005-0.013), whereas the change in label entropy tracked Swarm Gain (r = 0.74). Substituting alternative medium or large hospitals left network AUROC between 0.790 and 0.805. Conclusions. title: Near-Infrared Neuromodulation: Principles, Nanotechnology-Enabled Platforms, and Emerging Biomedical Frontiers.
desc: [ACS nano] Optogenetics enables highly specific regulation of neuronal activity with exceptional spatiotemporal precision, providing powerful tools for neural circuit interrogation and the treatment of neurological disorders. However, the limited tissue penetration of visible light restricts its application to deep neural tissues. Near-infrared (NIR) neuromodulation has emerged as a promising alternative by leveraging the superior tissue penetration and minimal invasiveness of NIR light. Recent advances in NIR-responsive nanomaterials, optical engineering, and neurotechnology have rapidly transformed the field from nonspecific photobiomodulation to cell-specific nanotransducer-mediated neuromodulation and integrated neuromodulation systems. In this review, we summarize the optical principles governing NIR propagation in biological tissues and the mechanisms underlying NIR-mediated neural stimulation. We then discuss recent advances in representative NIR nanotransducers, including photothermal, optoelectric, photoacoustic, and NIR-to-visible upconversion platforms together with integrated neuromodulation systems that combine NIR stimulation with multimodal neural recording and closed-loop feedback. We further highlight emerging applications in the central nervous system, optic nerve, and peripheral nerve disorders. Finally, we discuss the key challenges toward clinical translation, including improving tissue penetration, cell specificity, biosafety, and translation, developing intelligent multidisciplinary neuromodulation platforms, and integrating artificial intelligence with closed-loop neural interfaces to achieve adaptive, precise, and personalized neuromodulation.

title: MAGIC: Modality-Aware Gini Inspection for Clinical Hallucination Detection in LMMs
desc: Recent advances in medical large multimodal models (LMMs) have brought promising progress to clinical decision support, yet hallucination, the generation of confident but clinically unverifiable outputs, poses a critical threat to the reliability demanded in high-stakes medical settings. Existing hallucination detection methods, predominantly designed for unimodal settings, fail to capture the visual-linguistic dynamics inherent to medical imaging. We formulate the problem of hallucination detection in LMMs as disproportionate distribution of attention weights across the modalities during answer token generation. We quantify modality-specific attention concentration across layers and heads using the Gini coefficient and demonstrate statistically significant redistribution of attention mass between visual and textual tokens in hallucinated responses. We leverage these features to train a logistic regression-based classifier and evaluate it on two medical LMMs across three medical imaging modalities, demonstrating that our method achieves competitive or superior performance against contemporary hallucination detection baselines.

title: Beyond one-off training: Continuing support, system stability and worker-borne costs shape electronic community health reporting in Kisii County, Kenya
desc: Kenya's electronic community health information system (eCHIS) moves household and service data from community health promoters' phones into the national health information system. When reporting quality falls short, the usual response is more training and competency frameworks. We tested whether user capability and one-off training explain how well the system performs for its users, or whether continuing support and system stability matter more. We also examined where along the reporting chain quality was lost. In this convergent mixed-methods cross-sectional study in Kisii County, we surveyed 343 eCHIS users in 22 facility catchments, observed five sites against a structured checklist, and interviewed 13 key informants. Hierarchical ordinal and logistic regression with facility-clustered standard errors modelled user satisfaction and perceived system consistency. Formal eCHIS training was near universal (94.5%) and was not associated with either outcome. Adding continuing support (refresher training, mentorship and technical support response time) significantly improved both models. McFadden's pseudo-R{superscript 2} for consistency rose from 0.06 to 0.16. Each faster level of technical support response almost doubled the odds of reporting a consistent system (adjusted odds ratio 1.87, 95% CI 1.35-2.58). Each step up in crash frequency reduced the odds of higher satisfaction (0.60, 0.43-0.84). Digital comfort remained independently associated with both outcomes. At the observation sites, form logic secured completeness (all required fields were filled at 5 of 5 sites), but timeliness (2 of 5), consistency over time (1 of 5) and use of reports for decisions (0 of 4) failed, mostly because of synchronisation. In open-ended responses, 43.4% of respondents raised the cost of data bundles. Informants described promoters paying for connectivity and reinstalling the failing application themselves. Reporting quality depended less on what users knew than on the support around them. Competency frameworks will need matching standards for connectivity financing, support response and synchronisation monitoring.

title: Longevitomics as the Science of the Longevitome: Towards a Unified Systems Science of Healthy Longevity.
source: PubMed · Mechanisms of ageing and development
desc: [Mechanisms of ageing and development] The twenty-first century has transformed longevity research through genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, microbiome science, digital phenotyping and artificial intelligence. Yet healthy longevity remains difficult to explain because its determinants are commonly studied as separate molecular layers, mechanisms or biomarkers. Here, we introduce Longevitomics as an integrative systems framework for understanding, modeling and predicting healthy longevity and define the Longevitome inspired by the Latin expression vita longa (long life) as the dynamic architecture of biological, environmental and behavioral determinants that collectively shape psychosomatic resilience across the life course. We position this proposal in relation to the Hallmarks of Aging, geroscience, biological-age biomarkers, multi-omics and systems medicine. Longevitomics is not intended to replace these established frameworks or to constitute another molecular "ome." Rather, it provides a systems-level framework in which mechanistic hallmarks, multi-omic layers, physiological phenotypes, exposures and adaptive responses can be integrated longitudinally. We further consider how network analysis, causal inference, machine learning and digital-twin approaches may enable reconstruction of individual Longevitome trajectories and support a transition toward predictive and personalized longevity medicine.

title: Read and Ignore: What Self-Directed LLM Agents Do in Public Service Scenarios
desc: Underspecified instructions leave LLM agents to decide what to do. In public services, staff write these instructions, but the agent's decisions affect residents, patients, and students. We build four expert-validated public-service scenarios with records and decision levers that can be checked in the files, collect $2{,}400$ trajectories from ten LLMs under four prompt conditions, and compare them with $1{,}000$ runs in a context-free sandbox. Agents read the records in $96.9\%$ of open-ended runs and produce an artifact or a self-chosen task in $18.7\%$; with an explicit task, $86.0\%$ produce. Domain context does not change how many runs produce ($18.7\%$ vs.\ $16.0\%$), and the production ranking of the models largely carries over (Spearman $0.79$), while the ranking by whether a model reads the records does not ($0.19$). Context cuts boundary-probing turns per run by $60\%$, and some artifacts contradict the records. We contribute a test that a public-service institution can run on its own records before procurement; its rule-based taxonomy needs no labeled data, and scenarios, code, and trajectories are released.

desc: [Nihon Hoshasen Gijutsu Gakkai zasshi] To evaluate how output format affects inference accuracy in contrast-enhanced CT protocol generation using a large language model (LLM) combined with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) based on information obtained from a radiology information system. A total of 335 contrast-enhanced CT examinations with radiologist-determined protocols were retrospectively analyzed. Among them, 292 cases were used to build the RAG knowledge base, and 43 cases were used for validation. Two types of prompts were prepared: a structured format that outputs each imaging phase (unenhanced, arterial, portal venous, and equilibrium) in binary form (0/1), and a free-text format. The inference results generated by each format were evaluated. Complete agreement across all imaging phases was achieved in 16 of 43 cases (37.2%). Phase-specific accuracies were 76.2% for the unenhanced phase, 64.3% for the arterial phase, 78.6% for the portal venous phase, and 81.0% for the equilibrium phase. In the free-text evaluation, 65.1% of the generated contrast-enhanced CT protocols were rated as either "no issues" or "acceptable." An LLM integrated with RAG may serve as a potential decision-support tool for determining contrast-enhanced CT protocols.

title: An Asynchronous Federated Learning Platform for Lung Adenocarcinoma Grading via Foundation Models and Structural Pruning
desc: Classification of lung adenocarcinoma into poorly differentiated (PD) and well-to-moderately differentiated (WMD) subtypes plays an important role in patient survival; however, consistent classification is difficult due to inter-observer variability among pathologists. Collecting data from multiple hospitals is also challenging due to patient privacy concerns. This study proposes a web-based federated learning system that shares only locally trained model weights without sharing patient data between institutions. The UNI2 foundation model and CLAM-SB were used to classify pathological whole slide images. A four-client federated learning system was constructed, and the NLST cohort was reserved exclusively for external validation. In centralized evaluation, joint training with CPTAC and TCGA outperformed single-institution training on external validation, confirming the necessity of multi-institutional data integration. FedAvg, FedProx, FedBN, and FedNova were compared as federated learning algorithms under identical experimental conditions. Test AUC ranked as FedBN, FedProx, FedNova, and FedAvg. FedNova showed the most balanced classification performance between PD and WMD. L1-norm structural pruning at 20%, 30%, and 40% sparsity was applied to reduce model transmission size. FedAvg, FedProx, and FedBN showed a tendency of decreasing Test AUC under pruning, while FedNova achieved improved Test AUC across all sparsity levels. A web-based application was developed supporting slide upload, local training, AI classification, and attention heatmap-based visualization. The combination of FedNova and 40% pruning was confirmed as a practical approach that improves communication efficiency and classification performance while protecting patient privacy.

title: Could we see 10 Chinese Big Pharmas within a decade? Some CEOs think so
An adaptive multi-scale dilated convolutional neural network for arrhythmia detection.
source: PubMed · Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering
desc: [Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering] The rising global incidence of arrhythmia calls for reliable detection methods. Most existing approaches suffer from poor generalization and insufficient feature extraction for long-term electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. This work proposes an adaptive multi-scale dilated convolutional network (AMSDNet). It uses multi-scale dilated convolutions, gated adaptive weight allocation, and spatial attention fusion to capture global ECG features. Validated on Massachusetts Institute of Technology-Beth Israel Hospital Arrhythmia Database (MIT-BIH), the China Physiological Signal Challenge (CPSC) 2018, and the Computing in Cardiology Challenge (CINC) 2017 datasets, our method outperforms state-of-the-art models with average accuracy of 99.7%, 91.8% and 83.7%, respectively.

title: Interpreting Selective-Review Coverage for Head-and-Neck Auto-Contours
desc: Selective-review systems aim to reduce human review by passing candidates predicted to be low risk. However, coverage (the fraction passed) can be misleading when measurements needed to interpret risk are unavailable. We separate structural evaluability (a nonempty mask with all required measurements available), computational-endpoint status, and pass-or-review decisions using archived Mayo records and controlled OpenKBP analyses. In 3,968 Mayo records, all 1,167 recorded empty predictions (predicted target-organ masks containing zero voxels despite nonempty reference masks) were endpoint-negative and passed both modules, accounting for approximately 76% of each pass set. In a held-out OpenKBP test, a logistic-regression router achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.833 and average precision of 0.449 but passed all 544 non-evaluable candidates, including 542 prespecified empty-mask controls and 2 erosions that became empty. A structural gate removed those passes without changing scores or the threshold, preserved all evaluable passes, and assigned 98.71% of endpoint-positive candidates to review. Under the original preprocessing and in patient-disjoint development evaluation, a router trained only on evaluable candidates and a router modeling an unavailable state likewise passed no non-evaluable candidates, with similar evaluable discrimination and at least 99.0% of endpoint-positive candidates assigned to review in pooled outer-fold predictions. These results show that coverage should be interpreted jointly with candidate eligibility, endpoint scope, missingness handling, and routing rules; they do not establish clinical validity, deployment safety, or natural-failure prevalence.

AI-monitored bioadhesive for sutureless microvascular anastomosis.
desc: [Science (New York, N.Y.)] Microvascular anastomosis, the surgical suturing of small-caliber blood vessels, is technically demanding, time-consuming, and prone to failure from complications such as thrombosis. Existing adhesives are ineffective in the dynamic, wet surgical field, particularly for the limited cross-sectional interface of blood vessels. We present an integrated microneedle-interlocking adhesive system (iMAS) bioinspired by plant root anchoring. This platform combines a hydrophobic polymeric matrix with tetrahedral microneedles, creating robust, three-dimensional bonding for rapid, secure anastomosis. An embedded artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted wireless sensor enables continuous, real-time monitoring of vascular hemodynamics and cardiac graft health, facilitating predictive identification of complications such as stenosis and transplant rejection. In rat models, iMAS reduced procedural time by 78% and suppressed neointimal hyperplasia. iMAS streamlines microvascular anastomosis and enables proactive graft monitoring in transplantation.

title: Aggregate Accuracy Hides Diagnosis-Specific Failure in Medical Vision-Language Models
desc: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) are compared mainly by accuracy averaged across findings, a summary that can hide complete failure on a single diagnosis. We audit five open medical VLMs (MedGemma-4B, Lingshu-7B, HuatuoGPT-Vision-7B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and MedVLM-R1) on 6,048 ChestX-ray14 questions balanced by sex, age, finding, and label. On the 432 pneumothorax-positive X-rays, HuatuoGPT-Vision and Qwen2.5-VL detect zero cases while MedGemma and Lingshu detect 38% and 67% of the same images. The two failing models answer "no" to all 864 pneumothorax cases (balanced accuracy 0.500, chance), yet produce fluent, anatomically specific explanations that name the signs of a collapsed lung and then deny them, with no hedge or abstention. This failure is not an artifact of prompting, image resolution, label ambiguity, or model scale. It persists across four prompt formats, at native resolution, and on single-label cases. A within-model control shows the same forced prompt gives HuatuoGPT 79% recall on nodule but only 6% on pneumothorax. It survives a tenfold scale increase (Qwen2.5-VL-72B detects 4%) and replicates on SIIM-ACR, an independent dataset with radiologist-drawn masks, where the failing models detect 0 of 432 confirmed pneumothoraces, including 0 of the 144 largest lesions. Reading the models' logits and internal states shows this is not blindness. The two failing models are highly confident yet no better than chance and a linear probe recovers pneumothorax from their hidden representations even where recall is zero, so the finding is represented internally but suppressed at the output. Aggregate accuracy therefore cannot establish that a medical VLM can see a given finding, because a model that misses one can still describe it convincingly. Reporting per-finding recall and specificity on balanced cases is needed to tell the difference.

title: Writing, Speaking, and Thinking With AI: A Course Redesign in an Undergraduate Public Health Program.
desc: [Public health reports (Washington, D.C. : 1974)] Public health programs must prepare students to communicate effectively and use artificial intelligence (AI) responsibly. This case study describes the redesign of a communication course that advanced undergraduates take in a 2-year public health program. The redesign centered on 3 instructional priorities: maintain process approaches to writing, integrate explicit training in AI literacy, and expand oral assessments. While studying prompt engineering as part of AI literacy, students created their own AI writing tutor that provided feedback on clarity, organization, and tone. The AI writing tutors were restricted from completing the assignments on the students' behalf. Oral assessments included a "difficult conversation" about AI in health care and an interview with a health professional. The participants were 12 undergraduates who enrolled in the redesigned course in fall 2025. After completing their final assignments, the students answered a questionnaire with Likert-scale items and open-ended responses. The students perceived increases in their understanding of AI, confidence to use AI responsibly, and levels of preparation to use AI in future courses or professional settings. They indicated that AI tools in the redesigned course were advantageous for both writing and speaking assignments. For writing assignments, AI tools helped them brainstorm, organize, and revise. For speaking assignments, AI tools helped them prepare talking points and anticipate questions. Additionally, students identified challenges that they experienced in the redesigned course and provided recommendations for improvement. The findings suggest that the 3 instructional priorities can support student learning while strengthening assessment validity in AI-enhanced learning environments.

title: DETER: Suppression During Pretraining for Tamper Resistance
desc: Open-weight language models can acquire knowledge that could enable biological, chemical, or cyber misuse. Any attempt to limit such knowledge must remain effective after the model weights are released and can be fine-tuned. Unlearning applied after pretraining can be rapidly undone, whereas filtering the pretraining corpus offers greater resistance. We ask whether actively suppressing knowledge during pretraining can further increase the fine-tuning required to acquire it. Even simple gradient ascent interleaved with standard pretraining on the filtered corpus makes medical knowledge harder to acquire through adversarial fine-tuning than filtering alone or post-hoc unlearning. At 1B parameters, reaching the held-out PubMed loss of an unfiltered model requires over 20$\times$ as many PubMed fine-tuning tokens as after filtering alone. Retained knowledge is evaluated using both held-out data and downstream tasks. Across model sizes, varying suppression strength reveals an increasingly favorable trade-off between fine-tuning difficulty and held-out loss on retained pretraining data. These results point to pretraining as an effective stage for making unwanted capabilities harder to acquire through subsequent fine-tuning. Code is available at \href{https://github.com/MEGlr/DETER}{\texttt{github.com/MEGlr/DETER}}.

title: Large language model-assisted modern programming pedagogy model: a perspective on teaching programming in the era of LLMs.
desc: [Frontiers in artificial intelligence] Large language models (LLMs) are a double-edged technology. They can serve as learning assistants in programming while simultaneously raising pedagogical and ethical concerns. Programming education researchers have responded by providing guidelines and recommendations on teaching, assessment, and the ethical use of LLMs. Although these developments are welcome, the literature still lacks theory-based frameworks that provide a philosophical grounding for programming pedagogy. This perspective paper addresses this gap by proposing the LLM-Assisted Modern Programming Pedagogy (LAMPP) model. The model aims to provide a theory-informed framework for systematically guiding the integration of LLMs into programming pedagogy. It proposes four design principles encompassing the core components of pedagogy (i.e., teaching, lesson design, engagement, and assessment). Ethics is included as an additional dimension because ethical concerns cut across all aspects of pedagogy. The LAMPP model proposes different mechanisms that may mitigate potential learning losses associated with inappropriate or excessive reliance on LLMs. Future studies should test the effectiveness of these mechanisms. The model may provide a basis for educators, researchers, and policymakers when considering policies, curriculum structures, course outcomes, assessment practices, and ethical guidelines related to programming pedagogy. In summary, it is not about LLM tools themselves but about the pedagogical orchestration of these technologies in programming education.

title: Validation of a Facial-Video Digital Hydration Biomarker Score for Tracking Hydration State Transitions in a Real-World Fasting Model
desc: Hydration influences physiology and daily function, yet repeated practical measurement in everyday settings remains limited. We present initial real-world evidence that a facial-video lifestyle digital biomarker score can track the direction of hydration state transitions. Using Ramadan fasting as a model of prolonged fluid abstinence, we assessed whether the score tracks the transition between the fasting (pre-drink) state and the rehydrated (post-drink) state across three validation layers. In the primary cohort (104 participants, 208 videos), the score increased from a mean of 36.6 in the fasting (pre-drink) state to 70.6 in the rehydrated (post-drink) state (change = +33.9, 95% CI [+30.7, +37.1], p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 2.03), with 102 of 104 participants (98.1%) showing an upward shift. In a nested body-weight subgroup (20 participants), body weight increased by +0.74 kg after fluid intake (p < 0.001), confirming fluid uptake and providing supportive physical anchoring. In a nested serum osmolality subgroup (10 participants), osmolality decreased by -5.1 mOsm/kg (p < 0.001), with all post-drink values within the normal clinical range, providing exploratory biological support. An exploratory secondary comparison of water versus electrolyte rehydration showed no statistically significant difference in short-term score change (p = 0.247). This study does not establish a clinical diagnostic test for dehydration. Rather, these findings support the score as a lifestyle digital biomarker for tracking the direction of hydration state change in real-world settings.

title: Enhancing crop sustainability: GSEBNet for precise tomato leaf disease classification.
desc: [Frontiers in plant science] Plant diseases pose a major threat to food-supply sustainability. Early identification of crop diseases is crucial for agricultural production and crop yield. Classifying tomato leaves helps determine the treatments needed to keep crops healthy. Although many deep learning approaches have been proposed for plant disease classification, most rely on laboratory-captured images and struggle with real-field conditions. This study introduces an extensive class-based dataset collected in natural environments, visually distinguishing 13 infectious diseases and healthy tomato leaves. We propose the Gamma-preprocessed Squeeze-Excitation Block Network (GSEBNet), a lightweight CNN architecture that integrates Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) blocks with carefully configured Mobile Inverted Bottleneck Convolution (MBConv) layers and a domain-specific Gamma-Unsharp Brightness Reduction (GUBR) preprocessing pipeline. The model was trained and evaluated on a combined dataset of field-captured (PlantCity) and laboratory (PlantVillage) images covering 14 classes. The proposed GSEBNet achieved a test accuracy of 99.48% on the 14-class dataset, with precision, recall, F1-score, and Cohen's Kappa of 99.49%, 99.49%, 0.99, and 0.9944, respectively. The obtained results are competitive with those reported in previous studies, while acknowledging differences in datasets and experimental settings. The synergistic co-design of GUBR preprocessing with SE-enhanced MBConv layers significantly improves feature discriminability in low-quality field-captured images.

title: Discharge Summary Generation Is Not Just Summarization: A Reality Check for Evaluation
desc: Discharge summaries combine a retrospective account of hospitalization with discharge-time decisions. Physician-written references therefore contain both facts supported by prior clinical notes and reference-only content, potentially reflecting clinical synthesis, handoffs, or discharge planning. Reference-only evaluation can conflate failure to recover available information with failure to reproduce content absent from the model input. We introduce FairSumEval, an evidence-aware, fact-level framework that assesses whether each reference and generated fact is supported by the model's evidence and captured by the other summary. The resulting outcome map separates matches, omissions, and additions. Two complementary metrics, Soft IoU-S and Soft IoU-NS, measure reference-generation agreement for facts with and without identified evidence support. On 200 MIMIC-III admissions, 18.8% of physician reference facts have identified support in the prior evidence, compared with 65.4% and 63.5% of facts generated by a general-purpose and a medically specialized model. Overlap is substantially higher for supported content (0.255 and 0.236) than for content without identified support (0.030 and 0.026). The two scores are weakly correlated across admissions (rho = 0.22 and 0.17), and conventional metrics do not consistently capture both dimensions. FairSumEval distinguishes evidence-grounded summarization from agreement on content without identified support, revealing what models omit and add in each category.

title: Hierarchical supervised contrastive learning with AP-attention encoding for Wi-Fi fingerprinting indoor localization.
desc: [Frontiers in artificial intelligence] Indoor localization based on Wi-Fi fingerprinting has attracted significant research attention due to its infrastructure-free deployment and the ubiquitous availability of IEEE 802.11 access points (APs). A widely adopted deep learning architecture employs a stacked autoencoder (SAE) for unsupervised feature pre-training followed by a supervised multi-label classifier for hierarchical building, floor, and reference-point estimation. However, the SAE pre-training optimizes a mean squared error (MSE) reconstruction objective that is fundamentally misaligned with the downstream localization task, and it treats all 520 AP measurements uniformly despite many being uninformative at any given location. This study proposes HiSCL-AE, a two-component architectural modification: (1) an AP Importance Gate (AIG) that learns a per-AP sigmoid attention weight to adaptively suppress irrelevant APs end-to-end; and (2) a hierarchical supervised contrastive pre-training strategy (HiSCL) that replaces the MSE reconstruction objective with the supervised contrastive loss applied simultaneously at the building, floor, and reference-point granularities, directly optimizing the embedding geometry for localization. Experiments on the public UJIIndoorLoc benchmark demonstrate that HiSCL-AE achieves 90.73% building-floor accuracy and a mean positioning error of 11.38 m, outperforming the SAE baseline on both primary metrics (90.37% accuracy and 11.48 m error). Beyond accuracy, the AIG produces an interpretable AP importance map, revealing that fewer than 60 of 520 APs account for the majority of the discriminative signal-a finding with direct implications for radio map compression and network planning. We compared HiSCL-AE with six additional Wi-Fi fingerprinting methods under an identical experimental protocol; HiSCL-AE simultaneously achieves the highest Building+Floor accuracy and the lowest positioning error among the six methods compared.

title: Quantum-enhanced wafer failure prediction in semiconductor fabrication.
desc: [PloS one] In recent years, rapid advancements in semiconductor manufacturing have underscored the critical need for robust quality control to maintain high yields and reliability in wafer production. In this context, accurately predicting wafer failures plays a pivotal role across the industry in minimizing production losses and enhancing cost efficiency. However, despite the use of traditional machine learning and deep learning methods to predict wafer failures, they have failed to achieve the desired levels of accuracy. Consequently, the present study investigates the application of Quantum Machine Learning (QML) methods on the SECOM dataset. This dataset was balanced using the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE), wherein the QML models were implemented using the PennyLane library. In this study, comprehensive data pre-processing was performed on the SECOM dataset; subsequently, various QML algorithms such as Quantum Support Vector Machines (QSVM) and Quantum Random Forests (QRF) were implemented to classify wafers as 'good' or 'bad.' Although initial improvements in performance compared to traditional methods were modest, leveraging PennyLane's capabilities and fundamental principles of QML, this study highlights their transformative potential for industrial applications.

title: Design of Highly Efficient pegRNAs with Minimized Off-Target Effects Using DeepPrime.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Prime editors are newly developed genome editing tools capable of installing various types of mutations without introducing double-strand DNA breaks (DSBs) or requiring donor DNA templates. Prime editors consist of a Cas9 nickase fused to a reverse transcriptase (RT) domain and function as a ribonucleoprotein complex with prime editing guide RNA (pegRNA). Unlike the single guide RNA (sgRNA) used with Cas9 or base editors, the editing efficiency of pegRNAs is determined by the sequence composition and length of the guide sequence, primer binding site (PBS), and reverse transcription template (RTT). The high design flexibility of pegRNAs presents both opportunities and challenges. Therefore, designing pegRNAs with high efficacy has been a significant hurdle for the application of prime editing. Here, we present a step-by-step protocol for designing optimal pegRNAs to introduce desired edits using a deep learning-based algorithm, DeepPrime.

title: Nanofibrous Thermo-Optical Materials for Spacecraft Passive Thermal Control.
desc: [ACS applied materials & interfaces] Passive thermal control is essential for spacecraft operating in extreme extraterrestrial environments, where minimizing solar heat absorption while maximizing thermal radiation is critical for maintaining acceptable onboard temperatures without additional energy consumption. Here, electrospun nanofibrous materials, represented by a polymeric polytetrafluoroethylene:polyethylene oxide (PTFE:PEO) composite and ceramic silica, are introduced as a new class of lightweight spacecraft thermal control materials combining ultrahigh solar reflectance (or ultralow solar absorptance), strong infrared emittance, and environmental durability. Under flight-representative conditions in NASA's deep-space thermal simulator, including the cryogenic radiative background of deep space (<20 K), high vacuum (10-6 Torr), and AM0 solar irradiation (1367 W m-2), PTFE:PEO and silica nanofibers reached equilibrium temperatures of 143.2 and 137.4 K, respectively, compared with 281.4 K for aluminum foil. These values correspond to temperature reductions of 138.2 and 144 K, respectively, relative to aluminum foil. Complementary thermal modeling demonstrated that nanofibrous materials could reduce heat ingress relative to conventional multilayer insulation (MLI). Equivalent thermal performance could be achieved with substantially thinner and lighter nanofibrous insulation. Furthermore, the silica nanofibers showed about 60% greater resistance to atomic oxygen than Kapton, while thermal treatment significantly improved the atomic oxygen resistance of PTFE:PEO. These findings demonstrate the potential of electrospun nanofibrous architectures for passive thermal control of spacecraft and emerging space-based infrastructure, where favorable thermo-optical performance, environmental durability, and low mass are critical.
